draft.text: You came in because you have been coughing up blood, about three to four cups each day, and you have been short of breath for a few weeks.
You also mentioned you have lost about 10 pounds without trying and feel tired and have less of an appetite.
We found that you are a 57-year-old male who has not had any imaging tests like a chest X-ray or CT scan.
You have not had any chest pain or fever, but you have been having trouble getting appointments for blood tests or other care.
The doctor will arrange for you to have imaging tests like a chest X-ray or CT scan to look for the cause of the blood coughing.
Blood tests such as a complete blood count, coagulation profile, or tumor markers will also be done to check for possible issues with blood clotting or anemia.
You will need to come back for a follow-up after the results of these tests are available.

unverified_summary.text: You came in because you have been having shortness of breath and coughing up blood for a few weeks.
You also mentioned losing about 10 pounds without trying and feeling more tired than usual.
No specific findings were noted during the examination.
You are experiencing hemoptysis, which is coughing up blood, along with shortness of breath, weight loss, and fatigue.
Imaging tests like a chest X-ray or CT scan will be arranged to look for the cause of the coughing up blood.
